verdict: The 1.5 owned seconds within 15 wall seconds is the private caller completion heuristic, not an authored product timing contract. Original and V2 timing failures remain failures.

ownership.main: caps actual clock.getDelta at 0.25 s and forwards frameDt; held/gate-open frames supply zero
ownership.standing_horses: forwards the unchanged dt after distance/confidence/ancestor/document/reduced-motion/paused eligibility
ownership.owned_idle: accumulates only eligible host dt; consumes seeded initial rest, then multiplies by deterministic rate; no wall-clock catch-up or second adapter clamp

requirement_review: T2803 requires real portable/browser playback, update cost, grounded clips and lifecycle/gear interfaces; it states no 15-wall/1.5-owned target. The numerical target appears in the outside-app original caller line 97 and its HANDOVER.md.
permitted_conclusion: Observed current source-bound idle clock correctly accounts for the three actually forwarded eligible updates. This does not show an idle-clock defect in this sample.
separate_scope: A separately labeled loaded-host accounting check may compare actual eligible forwarded dt with source-defined elapsed, with original inputs/returns and gates preserved. Start from a fresh known-zero-age clone or account for rest already consumed. It must still separately measure source-clone isolation, head/tail displacement, hoof drift, pause/media/visibility, update cost and disposal; elapsed accounting alone does not qualify those.
